summary: H.R. 6010 extends temporary enhanced premium tax credits for health insurance through 2027 and alters income tiers and percentages. It modifies risk adjustment under Medicare Advantage by using two years of diagnostic data, excluding diagnoses from chart reviews and health risk assessments, and evaluating coding pattern differences. Additionally, the bill introduces new penalties, verification processes, consumer protections, and regulations for agents, brokers, and marketing organizations involved in health plan enrollments.

affected_groups.effect: Receive extended enhanced premium tax credits, consumer protections, and verification processes regarding agent-assisted enrollments.
affected_groups.group: Individuals purchasing health insurance through exchanges

affected_groups.effect: Subject to updated risk adjustment methodologies that evaluate coding patterns and use two years of diagnostic data.
Subject to stricter civil and criminal penalties for fraudulent applications, verification requirements for commissions, and expanded oversight and audits.
Subject to federal and state regulation regarding marketing materials, registration, and reporting of agent terminations.

key_provisions: Extends temporary premium percentages for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025, and before January 1, 2028, and adjusts household income eligibility tiers up to 600 percent of the poverty line.
Requires the Secretary to use two years of diagnostic data when available for Medicare Advantage risk adjustments starting in 2026.
Excludes diagnoses collected from chart reviews and health risk assessments from Medicare Advantage payment adjustment factors starting in 2026.
Establishes civil and criminal penalties for agents and brokers who provide incorrect, false, or fraudulent information on qualified health plan applications.
Mandates an enrollment verification process for federally operated exchanges to prevent unauthorized enrollments or changes made by agents or brokers.
Establishes criteria and oversight rules, including audits and marketing material restrictions, for field marketing organizations and third-party marketing organizations.
missing_information: The exact fiscal cost of extending the enhanced premium tax credits.
Specific regulatory start dates left to the discretion of the Secretary of Health and Human Services (within boundaries up to January 1, 2028).
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6010 extends temporary enhanced premium tax credits for health insurance through 2027 and alters income tiers and percentages. It modifies risk adjustment under Medicare Advantage by using two years of diagnostic data, excluding diagnoses from chart reviews and health risk assessments, and evaluating coding pattern differences. Additionally, the bill introduces new penalties, verification processes, consumer protections, and regulations for agents, brokers, and marketing organizations involved in health plan enrollments.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts health insurance affordability by extending tax credits, alters payment calculations for Medicare Advantage plans, and establishes significant regulatory and enforcement measures against fraudulent enrollment practices by brokers and marketing entities.

title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend and modify the enhanced premium tax credit, and for other purposes.
